places.name: The Porch
places.description: Laid-back gathering place for seasonal menus crafted using ingredients from local producers.
places.narrative: Sitting right at the edge of Schenley Park, this farm-to-table spot serves seasonal menus with local ingredients — reviewers mention wagyu burgers and note "everything on the menu sounded good." Photos show colorful salad bowls and plated entrees with rice and meat, plus a polished patio with large shade trees. At 4.1 with 2,130 reviews, the rating is the lowest among close-by options — service seems to be the common gripe. Open until 8 PM, just 3 min away, with live music, full bar, and coffee. The park-adjacent location is the selling point — pair it with a Schenley walk.

evidence.text: Everything on the menu sounded good
I ordered the wagyu burger and fries and my friend got the grilled cheese and tomato soup
But once we received our food and drinks that's the last we seen our server

reviews.text:
This is a very nice restaurant.  Looks clean and cozy.  Everything on the menu sounded good. I ordered the wagyu burger and fries and my friend got the grilled cheese and tomato soup.  The good looked good and tasted delicious.  But once we received our food and drinks that's the last we seen our server.  No check ins or refills.  That was disappointing.
Table had 5 plates 5 sets of silverware and 5 glasses on it when we sat down.  They were never removed.  Sat on the table our whole visit.

Went to The Porch for brunch and I’m glad we did. Right on the campus of the University of Pittsburgh this place is a definite recommendation. We decided to get a pitcher of the Bloody Mary and it did not disappoint. The food was fabulous with multiple seasonal options. For a light lunch the salmon wrap was fantastic with a great flavor profile. Parking took a little while to find however after finding street parking the meal made the walk over worth it.

This is overall a phenomenal spot for lunch or dinner, located right on Pitt's campus. The restaurant has a modern feeling, with both indoor and outdoor seating overlooking a bright green field of grass. Menu is varied, with something to please just about anyone. The restaurant was very clean, and the staff was friendly as well. With fair pricing on top of this, it is hard to say no.

We came hear to eat with a bunch of people (~20) after a conference at CMU. We had our own two tables. The place was buzzing, but it was still quiet enough to talk. The food itself was excellent. Service was kind and attentive.

I went several weeks ago and had the most wonderful server for brunch named Isabella. She was so friendly and kind and knew so much about the menu. I told her I like to eat a lot and she recommended the butternut squash pizza with prosciutto. OMG, it was SO delicious. Thank you Isabella for the great service and amazing recommendation! 🍕

places.name: Burghers Brewing Co.
places.narrative: A Lawrenceville pub that's essentially all outdoors — reviewers flatly state "there is really no indoor seating" and warn it's tough in extreme weather. Photos show a charming courtyard between industrial brick buildings with umbrella-covered tables, planters, and open sky, plus burger baskets and loaded fries. Beer only — no cocktails or wine. Dog-friendly, open until 8 PM today, 6 min away. Great on a nice day, but have a backup plan since there's essentially no indoor fallback if weather turns. The outdoor-only setup is either a feature or a bug depending on conditions.

evidence.text: There is really no indoor seating
So if it’s very cold or hot, it would be a little hard to eat here
I liked the food and service was very nice

reviews.text:
There is really no indoor seating. So if it’s very cold or hot, it would be a little hard to eat here . They have benches that are covered, very small indoor area, and a bathroom. Water or soft drinks come in bottle/can.
I liked the food and service was very nice. We got the liberty smash burger 🍔. Fries were good too. Overall I really liked the concept and their food! $50 for two people including tip.

I just had the best meal and beers here. The beer garden concept is great too! They have a tv outside where a game could be put on. The brewmaster really knows what he is doing because everything was very close to Bavarian favorites that I enjoy in Europe. The staff was very friendly too! The burger was amazing, and I never knew I was missing out with pierogis on the side. Loving it here! I will be back!

Wow, Burghers was amazing! We enjoyed lunch here after a campus tour at Duquesne University. The BBBG team took time to understand my food allergies. They prepared my meal with care and kindness! The Green Tree Bowl was delicious and safe. My family thoroughly enjoyed their burgers and fries. The garden and music selection perfectly complimented the experience. Thank you!!

We had a smashing good time at Burghers Beer Garden with Brittany! It was our 2nd stop on a brewery tour and it was by far the best! We sampled all 10 beers + a bonus beer. They were all excellent. The burgers, fries & pierogis were delicious. And the service was top notch. I only wish we were not out of towners and could make this our regular hang out.

If you’re on a never-ending quest for the best smash burger like I was, STOP RIGHT NOW — the burger gods have answered. We hit up this convenient little burger spot and it was everything: food hot ash, right iff the grill…. music so good you almost forget you’re stuffing your face, and customer service that felt like being welcomed by an old friend who also happens to know their way around a flat top grill.

We got two Oakland burgers (smashed to absolute perfection), fries so crispy they could be  ASMR content, Joe’s Peach Tea (elite), a bottle of classic Root Beer (Red Ribbon knows what’s up), mojo sauce, AND burgher sauce. Picky boyfriend approved — and trust me, that’s harder to accomplish than finding a parking spot in Southside on a Saturday night.

The person running the place? Cool as hell. The type of cool where you instantly want to be friends. We didn’t just eat — we demolished every last crumb. If you leave even a fry behind, you’re doing life wrong.

Final Verdict:
10/10. Best smash burger I’ve had after months of searching.
“Oh yea we’re definitely coming back…” words of the picky boyfriend (2 bites in)

Photos show a cozy courtyard with wooden picnic tables and string lights between buildings, plus close-ups of dark beers alongside hand pies. At 4.8 with 34 reviews, it's small but the flexibility to grab great takeout and pair it with their craft beer is genuinely appealing. Open until 7 PM today, 9 min away.

reviews.text:
My favorite brewery in this city. They have something for everyone but this time of year is my favorite beer.
The hallowed ground  pumpkin ale is my all time favorite, with the gingerbell coming in 2nd.  My boyfriend likes all sours.
The location is easy to park with a private lot behind the building and they allow you to bring in your own food. The patio/beer garden is great in the summer to bring games and pizza and hang out. We love this place and will always return.
We went for the Mario kart tournament. First time there and everyone was so friendly and the beer is great. They have pretzels but can bring food!

I enjoyed my time here. They serve up brews and have other events like trivia and chili cookoffs (there is no food here otherwise). Service was great and the brews are better than what I've had at other places. They also have a patio for when it's warmer. I'd come back when in the area
Have only been a few times but the staff are always incredibly welcoming and the beer is always solid with a great variety.
Really chill. Had a guy playing an accordion for the evening. Nothing but vibes.

places.name: Hazelwood Brew House
places.narrative: A stunning Hazelwood multi-brewery complex in a historic building — reviewers describe a ground-floor outdoor tasting area, a third-floor tap room, AND a rooftop beer garden with "a great view." Photos confirm a dramatic elevated deck overlooking tree-lined hillsides — easily the most scenic outlook on this entire list. Multiple breweries under one roof plus comfort food (photos show chicken tenders and fries). At 4.9 with 109 reviews, open until 6 PM today, 7 min away. That rooftop with those views is a genuine wow-factor destination you won't find elsewhere.

evidence.text: There is a small, outdoor tasting area on the ground floor for all 3 spaces and then a larger 3rd floor tap room for all 3 spaces, plus a rooftop beer garden
Great outdoor space with a rooftop area with a great view, additional floors that will be open soon, and a dog-friendly patio when you first walk up
They had a food truck while we were there, so you can get a bite to eat, too

reviews.text: Here at Hazelwood Brew House is Abstract Brew Company and New France Brewing Company. There is supposed to be a 3rd Brewing Company in this complex, but sadly they have closed entirely. They are hoping to have a 3rd in Q1 2025. Both offer a wide variety of brews. I enjoyed the Blindfold Belgian Tripel at New France and the Killer Cobra Imperial Cream Ale at Abstract. Awesome location. There is a small, outdoor tasting area on the ground floor for all 3 spaces and then a larger 3rd floor tap room for all 3 spaces, plus a rooftop beer garden. Definitely worth checking out.

Just came across this today, and it did not disappoint. Three breweries in one really cool space. Great outdoor space with a rooftop area with a great view, additional floors that will be open soon, and a dog-friendly patio when you first walk up. The brew house is located right off the bike path, easily accessible from Hot Metal Bridge. They had a food truck while we were there, so you can get a bite to eat, too. Looking forward to biking here and enjoying the space again!

The space is awesome. Water cups on the way out! Good thinking.

La France had beers I really liked; Abstract Realm had a tasty stout. Abjurgation is on deck; sent a message to get a ballpark date but no response yet.

It will be very interesting to see what kind of food options they'll add.

The Hazelwood Brewhouse is a beautiful space with great views and two (previously three) decent breweries plus a comfort food place. It is MASSIVELY overbuilt and not very well known— as a result, pints run $8-10 on average. Still worth checking out for a drink before heading to Hazel Grove.

If you want a fun evening with friends, this is the place to go. There are 2 micro breweries serving totally different styles of beer. 1 has wonderful lagers. We had the MaiBock, smooth and on point.  The other brewery had a refreshing oatmeal coconut stout.
We had the steak salad with arugula greens dressed in a light vinegarette, while our friends had the mac & cheese and nachos.
We were also there for trivia night. We came in 4th... but 3 teams were tied for first. Does that make us second place? Not sure. Check out the roof top also while you are there.

places.narrative: A North Side brewery where reviewers praise "great atmosphere, beer, and music" and note food comes via rotating trucks and popup events throughout the week. At 4.7 with 108 reviews, open until 6 PM today, but 11 min away. Beer-only drink menu. The food truck model means you'll want to check what's rolling today before committing to the drive. A solid community brewery that rewards the trip when the stars align — good truck, good weather, good company.

evidence.text: Throughout the week they have food trucks or popup food events
Great location on the North Shore
Cool indoor relaxed space with some comfy couches and pinball and a newly added outdoor patio

reviews.text: This is a really cool local bar on the Northside. The beers are all made in-house and taste amazing. You can sit at the bar or in the back where there are couches and pinball machines. Throughout the week they have food trucks or popup food events.

Great location on the North Shore. Cool indoor relaxed space with some comfy couches and pinball and a newly added outdoor patio. The beer line up is solid. They have lots of different styles, and all have been on point. They don't have food, but food trucks are sometimes on site. They also offer pitchers of beer, which is rare for breweries. Four packs available to go.

Went down to the northside to go to War streets brewing (Piers Pub) and happily found that Four points opened a taproom within a block.
Four points had 10 different beers with pretty much something for everyone. I had two IPAs and both were outstanding. I particularly liked the “Kids” IPA, around 5.5% and very hazy.
The place was large with lots of room to move around and they had an outdoor space.
It’s pretty cool that there’s three breweries within one block of each other, Four points, War Street brewing, and 412.

Four points has quickly moved into our favorite brewery to visit in the city. We haven’t had a beer we don’t like and the bartenders have been incredible each time, so kind! Also have appreciated that they’ve been family friendly. Being newly postpartum, you hope to find spaces you used to enjoy that still work for your family - and they have been nothing short of amazing in making us feel we belong. Great atmosphere, beer, and music - can’t go wrong!

The best part about this place is that they offer Surfside spiked teas. I don’t drink beer and I am always so happy when a brewery serves Surfsides!!! Thank you! Oh and my husband says the beer is really good.

places.name: Aslin Beer Company
places.narrative: The Strip District outpost of the Virginia-born brewery chain, where reviewers recommend grabbing "an outside table before 5 PM" for "a beautiful view of the city" and highlight happy hour slider deals. Photos show colorful poke bowls and wings with dipping sauce — the in-house kitchen (not just trucks) is a genuine differentiator. At 4.0 with 354 reviews, it's the lowest-rated actual brewery on this list, which is notable. Open until 10 PM today, 8 min away. The food and views are the draw here, even if the overall experience doesn't quite match the competition.

evidence.text: Happy hour deals are great (a bunch of sliders for $10 and huge beers), and it’s got a beautiful view of the city
If you can get here before 5pm and grab an outside table, it’s the spot to be in the strip
Really good food options for a brewery spot

reviews.text: This is THE spot. Happy hour deals are great (a bunch of sliders for $10 and huge beers), and it’s got a beautiful view of the city. Would love to see a happy hour rotation of one of their stronger beers every now and then, but that’s just me being picky. If you can get here before 5pm and grab an outside table, it’s the spot to be in the strip. Love it

Really good food options for a brewery spot! Their pizza is thin crust, crispy with some nice topping combination options. Brussels sprouts were also worth it, actually crispy with a nice sauce too. The only kinda miss was the fries, which weren’t really crispy and were just okay, but would say the pizza is worth trying!

I visited this place for the first time with a few friends, located inside the new Strip District Terminal. We were lucky to find parking right outside the terminal. Although we wanted outdoor seating, we ended up inside, which was a fun experience with great music.

The beer selection was fantastic and enjoyable, with plenty of options to choose from. We ordered pizza—the pepperoni and ricotta was a big hit with our group, though the buffalo chicken didn’t win everyone over.

I liked that we could order through ToastTab, and the food and beer were brought out quickly! The system was easy to use, and you can keep the tab open to add more items—perfect for large groups so you can order separately.

However, one major downside was that the indoor area was super cold—it was almost uncomfortably chilly! Definitely bring a jacket if you’re planning to sit inside. Overall, a great spot, but they really need to address the indoor temperature.

The food is decent but I suspect it would improve if they limited their menu. Pizza, burgers, Korean options, and pasta is possibly too many options to deliver uniformly great outcomes.

The sliders were mediocre at best; it was a full-size patty cut into quarters. Just remove sliders from the menu, in my opinion, if this is going to be how you expand your menu. The mushroom pizza was good but not great. Too much crust. The hot dog was decent and I recommend it.

The carry-out can selection on November 28, 2025 consisted of many passable cans and only one DIPA; it almost seems like a conglomerate of their less-enticing 12oz distro beers and the less-popular one-offs from the past few months. Another DIPA would have been nice. Perhaps a stout.

I love fest bier and Märzen lager, but still available for carry-out in the last three days of November?  I suspect the administration is potentially struggling with projecting demand. In their defense, it must be tough in a town that has a segment that loves light beer but another that prefers barrel-aged stouts. And many others.

There were no draft BA-stouts on November 28. Or any (alcoholic) stouts.

Staff is great; very nice. The drinks arrive fast.

We will come back, but we liked the options better November 2024.

Really lovely interior and nice seating outside.  And the staff bring you drinks really fast.

The drinks aren't the best (a little sour for my taste, but that's subjective and you might like them).  They aren't that expensive, though.  The food is a bit pricey.

There's one main negative experience I've had here.  I took my family from out of state to Aslin because it was one of my favorite breweries due to the location/vibe.  A couple of us were getting beers + food there sitting at one of the outdoor tables.  My little sister has a severe dairy allergy, so her and some other folks got some food from a restaurant down the street that doesn't use any milk products.  To be fair to Aslin: there are notes on the outdoor tables saying no outside food.  And our waiter didn't know about the allergy.  But when one of the staff brought out a drink, they forced us to leave or throw away the food.  It left a bad taste in my mouth and I haven't been back since.

places.name: Burghers Brewing Co. Millvale
places.narrative: The Millvale sibling of Burghers Brewing, where reviewers praise comfort food staples — "the food is fantastic, the beer is cold, and the atmosphere is relaxed but fun." Mac and cheese and pierogies get mentions, though the cheese-heavy comfort food is tricky for Carissa and Ashi. At 3.9 with 97 reviews, the rating is among the lowest here. Open until 8 PM today, 8 min away. Not a destination, but if you're in Millvale and hungry, it'll do the job.

reviews.text:
With four locations across the city 📍, Burghers has carved out a reputation for delicious smash burgers and craft beers!!! ✨✨✨The Millville location is the newest and by far the coolest—it’s got a laid-back, yet modern vibe, with the added bonus of brewing their own beer right on-site.🙌🏽
I went with the Pittsburgh Smashburger, and it was a total game-changer. This burger comes stacked with cheddar, crispy onions, tangy pickles, creamy coleslaw, and crispy fries all drizzled in a house-made burgher sauce. 🍔 Every bite was packed with flavor, and the combination of textures was spot-on. Highly recommend it if you're in the mood for something hearty and satisfying.
Beyond the burgers, they also nails comfort food staples like mac & cheese and pierogies, giving you a great balance of flavors if you’re in the mood for something a little different. 🤌🏽The craft beer selection is top-notch, with something for every taste, making it the perfect pairing for their smash burgers.🍺
All in all,  Burghers is a must-visit. The food is fantastic, the beer is cold, and the atmosphere is relaxed but fun. Whether you’re in the mood for a casual meal or just looking to grab a drink with friends, this place has you covered.

Exceptionally clean, and well designed and the food was excellent!

Craft beer can become a "dart at the dartboard" kind of blah experience where you try a few then start pining for a Yuengling; here every beer we tried was fantastic. Ended up settling on Knob & Tube Hazy Pale Ale

The smash burger was excellent and you'd think - an $8 hit dog? Get out! Yet it was brilliant and it's going to be my go-to if I can't handle a full burger

The Mac and cheese was savory, with beer cheese; next time we're going to request a side of beer cheese to go with the fries

Recommend this, their newest and apparently flagship location. Park out back and you can take a short walk straight into their second floor:

Again the place is a showcase of well thought-out design, and the food worth the excursion!

Was a little unsure about going here for Oktoberfest. It seemsclike more of a corporate brewery, but I'm glad I did.

The beer is really good, and the food was great as well. Probably the best potato pancakes I've had! (Tbf, I'm not a huge fan of potato pancakes, but these were good.) The gravy and mustard was very authentic and delicious, the curry ketchup was a nice touch for their fries.

It's a big open space, with plenty of seating. Very clean and welcoming. Parking is typica for the area, small lot and street parking, but plenty of on street parking mid day weekend when we came.

(Sorry, no pics of food, I was hungry!)

The only small annoyance was some newer staff that weren't quite up to speed, but still friendly and accommodating, and this seems to be the rule, not the exception these days, so be patient, we're all in this together!

Can't wait to come back and try their burgers!

While the food was good, I can't say that I considered it good value for money. I wasn't sure what the size situation was so I didn't pay the upcharge to go from mini to normal, because surely they aren't charging me $13.50 for a child-sized chicken sandwich, right? That's a regular entree price for enough food to leave hungry, right? Well, that was my mistake, but it's thankfully one I only have to make once.

Had the Maggie’s Farm with the mushroom and beef blend burger.  It was fantastic.  Washed it all down with a house brewed German-style Pilsner, which was also spot on.  Partner had the impossible burger, which she said was outstanding.  They clearly know what they are doing with burgers and beer.   Will definitely be back.

places.name: Late Addition Brewing + Blending
places.narrative: A North Side brewery where reviewers confirm "seating available inside and outside" and note the outdoor space "was already nice." Photos show a pleasant patio with picnic tables, umbrellas, and gravel ground surrounded by a wood fence, plus sidewalk seating at the brick building. Photos also show chicken tenders and fries. At 4.4 with 50 reviews, open until 6 PM today, but 11 min away. A fine neighborhood spot, but at that distance there are stronger options closer to home.

evidence.text: Seating available inside and outside
The outdoor space hasn't changed, but it was already nice
Also they offer some NA and non-beer options, which is great

reviews.text: Cool taproom & brewery with lots of delicious craft brew options. Seating available inside and outside.

I really like the rebranding of this brewery. The space feels cozy and inviting. The outdoor space hasn't changed, but it was already nice. Really enjoying seeing newer styles on the list. Also they offer some NA and non-beer options, which is great.   Looking forward to going back.

Late Addition is a cool spot to grab a beer. Everything they have on tap is crisp and refreshing. We tried a few sour beers and they were great. The inside is also cool with the stained wood walls and exposed joist ceiling.

My friend and I unfortunately had what turned out to be an unpleasant and angering experience involving the bartender and another patron there recently. My friend was already there and spoke highly of the place before I arrived. We were hoping to find a bar that was quiet and intimate where we could just have a pint and chat. When I arrived it was just my friend and the male bartender. The beer was excellent. I had the German lager. My friend liked his. The bartender was friendly with us and seemed to appreciate our patronage and money. Then, the bartender's whole demeanor and attitude changed toward us from friendliness and appreciation to snootiness and mockery after his dude bro friend with a dog came in. The dude bro started giving my friend looks like he was sizing him up for a fight. Both he and the bartender started laughing at my friend's expense when he was talking to me. I asked both the bartender and his dude bro friend if there was a joke that I was supposed to get that I was missing and they both denied that they were laughing at him. My friend and I had trivia at another bar to go to at 6pm. Though it was early (around 5:30) seats fill fast at the other bar on trivia night, so we decided to leave early. He was also trying to keep his anger in check the whole time they were laughing at him because he usually goes right to using his fists when grown adults have acted like the bartender and his buddy have acted that way around him in the past. We left politely but will not be back. We've seen Late Addition dead more than once while neighboring bars are hopping with patrons. If the bar is hiring snob bartenders who are perfectly okay with mocking paying customers with their dude bro friends, then it's not much of a surprise that the bar is empty.

Visited Late Addition Saturday January 17th. Probably should of listened to the customer exiting as we entered who said sarcastically "highly recommend!!". But we entered and immediately it felt like the bartender was annoyed at us coming into the establishment and asking for samples, as if we were interrupting something!  But we sampled and ordered full pours and upon settling the tab he loudly commented about the tip... TWICE.. and after the second time he told us to not to come back! Would of given 0 star if possible!

Would never go back and will be sure to tell anyone visiting the area to pass on this place and go to Four Points or Lefty's.

places.name: Back Alley Brewing Company
places.full_address: 2975 W Liberty Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15216, USA
places.narrative: Way out in Dormont at 16 min away — the most distant open option on this list. The 4.8 rating from 92 reviews is strong, with reviewers praising staff warmth and noting "there is typically a food truck outside too." No outdoor photos captured despite outdoor seating being listed. Open until 8 PM today. At this distance, you'd need a specific reason to choose it over closer options unless you're already on that side of town.

reviews.text: This is such a fun location to visit! Bright and airy inside with a wide range of beers on tap to enjoy. There is typically a food truck outside too.

We rented Back Alley Brewing for a shower, and it was perfect! Lots of natural light, lots of tables, the cutest greenery draped across the ceiling, super friendly staff that was wonderful to work with, pretty affordable. Highly recommend! And I know I already said this, but Lee was just great to work with. He was responsive to emails, easy-going, and friendly. We rented out the right side of the brewery, which is a pretty segmented off room (but without doors). Our group was just under 40 people, and it was comfortable.

Back Alley Brewing is a very nice little brewery. We hosted my wife's 40th birthday party there and it was the perfect space for about 30 people. I think you could have up to 40 somewhat comfortably. The beers were really good. I'm not an IPA guy so I had the coffee stout and the lager; both very good! I highly recommend this place to have a few beers or to have a get-together.

We rented out Back Alley for our daughters birthday party and I highly recommend it for anyone looking for a great event space with flexibility and good beer! The Back Alley team was super accomodating and communicative throughout the process. The beer was excellent and the bartenders was incredibly attentive and helpful.

Fabulous brewery. Came into town Saturday and this was first stop. Loved the Goldenrod Autumn Shandy and bought a 4pack to go of the Back Alley IPA. Enjoyed this little gem of a brewery so much we went back Sunday too. My husband and I shared 2 flights so we could try nearly all of their beers. Fluffernut pumpkin beer was also very good. Will definitely be back next time we're in Pittsburgh. Beers are solid

places.description: Upbeat spot offering build-your-own burgers & other locally sourced fare, plus shakes & sodas.
places.narrative: The Lawrenceville Tap House sibling of Burghers Brewing, focused on build-your-own burgers with locally sourced ingredients plus shakes and sodas. Here's the dealbreaker: outdoor seating is listed as unavailable, which misses the query entirely. Reviewers gripe about pricing — "prices don't match the menu." Photos show pulled pork sandwiches. At 4.2 with 692 reviews, it's decent but indoor-only. Full bar with cocktails, wine, and coffee, open until 8 PM, 6 min away. Only works as a rainy-day backup.

reviews.text: Good food. Watch your receipt. Prices don't match the menu. I ordered the morningside $15 with chilli mac $4 charged $20. Originally server didn't give me fries. The menu clearly states "upgrade your fries." I took the dollar discrepancy out of the tip.

The least busiest of the breweries we visited, but it was the most interaction we got with staff, a big plus in my book...

From the outside it was non-desript, but the inside revealed a sizeable taproom/restaurant setup with a decent sized bar to go along with it all.  Though we did not eat here, we could see they had a nice sized menu and it was made to order.

For beers we had each a lager and a dunkel, very good offerings that came in nice cone-shaped glassware - definitely out of the ordinary.  Service was spot on and super friendly as we shared our experiences on the day and they genuinely were receptive to the whole discussion.

Though it was a little hard to find, it was worth the effort and definitely worth a return trip..

Stopped by to pass some time.  Tried the Aufstoin. Awesome doughy malt lager.  Tried the grilled cheese.  Was great four kinds of cheese on toast with a tomato and pickles.  Added pickled onions.  Yummy.

Also have had blended mushroom beef patty burgers and the fries never disappoint.

This was probably the best smash burger I have had in the city! The flavors were off the charts and the fries had the perfect crisp on them. Our waitress was very kind and attentive to our needs. We were there earlier in the afternoon so it wasn’t too busy which was nice. Would highly recommend checking this spot out!

Burgh'ers in Lawrenceville is a great place for burgers and beer. It's a casual, industrial spot with friendly staff.
I had the Oakland burger and it was perfectly cooked and included locally sourced toppings.
I didn't try any of the beers, but they had an impressive selection with house brewed options.
You can also get a Mini Smash if you have less of an appetite.

places.name: Spoonwood Brewing Company
places.narrative: Arguably the best overall brewery-with-patio package on this list when it's open — reviewers praise both food and atmosphere, with attentive service called out by name. At 4.5 with 841 reviews, it's well-proven and people seek it out. Two big catches: it's closed today (Sunday) and it's 20 min away in Bethel Park — the furthest option on the list. Bookmark this for another day when you can make the drive and they're serving.

reviews.text: Brunch this morning at Spoonwood Brewing was wonderful! The Eggs Benedict was perfectly cooked and the hollandaise sauce was delicious. My husband and I shared the Waffle of the Day - the Cinnamon Toast Crunch. Surprisingly it wasn’t overly sweet. It was an airy, wonderful waffle. Cindy was our wait staff and she was friendly, attentive and even brought cinnamon sticks for my chai tea. Our food server, Trish, was quick, thorough and helpful. Take home an growler of beer for later, too! Excellent brunch!

We had a lovely Sunday brunch. The staff was professional, attentive and personable. Our meals were delicious and I can’t say enough about the potable potions we had with our meal. Great food and fun atmosphere. A gem in Bethel Park.
Great beers, space, service and food! Very spacious, cool vibes, many TVs for sports viewing and nice looking outdoor section. Will come back when in the area :)
The Jam Burger was tasty and cocktail menu (rainbow marg specifically) was delicious! Exceptionally busy on a Saturday night with no parking. The earlier you get there the better!

Never had a bad meal here. And the selection of beer is great. We are not into IPA's and many other places we've been to tend to have more of them, whereas Spoonwood offers a bigger variety.  My favorite by far was the Secret Alphabet made with honey, oranges,  jalapeño and habenero peppers.
